The Epistemological Spiral
Human knowledge is not
(or does not follow) a
straight line, but a curve,
which endlessly
approximates a series of
circles, a spiral.
Dialectics provides an
immeasurably rich content
compared to 'metaphysical'
materialism, whose
fundamental misfortune is its
inability to apply dialectics to the
process and development of
knowledge.

The Architecture of Idealism
A fragment of the curve
transformed one-sidedly into
an independent, complete,
straight line.
From the standpoint of dialectical
materialism, philosophical idealism is
not mere nonsense.
It is a one-sided, exaggerated
development (inflation, distension) of
one feature of knowledge into an
absolute, divorced from matter and
nature.
The Result:
Rectilinearity, one-sidedness,
woodenness, and petrification. This
tangent leads into the quagmire of
clerical obscurantism.

The Sterile Flower
Clerical obscurantism (= philosophical idealism), of course, has
epistemological roots, it is not groundless; it is a sterile flower undoubtedly,
but a sterile flower that grows on the living tree of living, fertile, genuine,
powerful, omnipotent, objective, absolute human knowledge.
